tests: Large but simple: 1.1 million monthly users, read-mostly cached feeds, no accounts, two part-time people, no on-call. Maturity must come from stakes and team, not user count (never large); the 'large-scale platform' label is contradicted by the brief; Ashford's 400,000 users are projected; the agency's 2-minute alert term, the location-stays-on-phone promise and the $30,000 cap are constraints; rush-hour reliability, hosting cost and maintenance time are ranked goals.

product.summary: A phone app showing nearby bus and tram departures and live delays for three cities, from transit agencies' open data feeds.

source.quote: NextStop is a phone app that shows bus and tram departures for three cities
We have run NextStop for six years.

evidence.value: 1.1 million monthly users, flat for two years

source.quote: It has 1.1 million monthly users and about 180,000 daily users, and these numbers have been flat for two years.

evidence.value: Backend is two small services and a cache, run by two part-time people

source.quote: the backend is two small services and a cache, and it is boring on purpose
It has 1.1 million monthly users
about 180,000 daily users

observed.what: transit feeds polled and cached; almost all traffic is reads

source.quote: Almost everything is reading: departure times and delays come from the transit agencies' open data feeds, which our backend polls every 30 seconds and caches.

projected.what: user numbers expected to stay as they are (flat for two years)

source.quote: these numbers have been flat for two years
On weekdays between 7am and 9am, and again between 4pm and 7pm, requests run at about 5 times the daily average.
On snow days we have seen 10 times the average for a whole morning.

availability.value: Must work during rush hour; night outages go unnoticed

source.quote: During rush hour the app has to work: an outage at 8am means thousands of one-star reviews and angry emails to the agencies. At 2am nobody notices.

data_loss_tolerance.value: No user data to lose; everything can be fetched again from the feeds

source.quote: There is no user data to lose; everything we show can be fetched again from the feeds.

recovery_time.value: Night failures wait until morning (no on-call)

source.quote: We are not on call; if something breaks at night, it waits until morning.
We collect no names, emails or accounts.

data_categories.value: phone location, used on the phone only

source.quote: The app uses the phone's location to find nearby stops, and the location never leaves the phone
We keep anonymous usage counts for 90 days.

data_categories.value: device advertising identifier, passed to the ad network

source.quote: Our ad network receives the device's advertising identifier.

source.why: No accounts or names; location stays on the phone; only anonymous counts and an advertising identifier leave it.

source.quote: We keep anonymous usage counts for 90 days.

sharing.value: ad network receives the device's advertising identifier

source.quote: Our ad network receives the device's advertising identifier.

jurisdictions_or_rules.value: published privacy policy promises location never leaves the phone

source.quote: we say so in our privacy policy and we intend to keep that promise

requirements.value: no sign-in and no user accounts

source.quote: Users do not sign in.
NextStop is run by the two of us, Ines and Rafael.
Ines writes the Swift and Kotlin apps
Rafael writes the Go backend and looks after the servers

operating_capacity.value: about one day a week each, beside a consulting business

source.quote: We also run a consulting business, so NextStop gets about one day a week from each of us.
We are not on call

build.value: $30,000 for this rework, no more this year

source.quote: We can put $30,000 into this rework, and not more this year.

run_monthly.value: hosting $2,300 a month against about $9,000 a month of ad revenue

source.quote: Ads bring in about $9,000 a month. Hosting costs $2,300 a month

constraints.text: Show Riverton's service alerts within 2 minutes of publication (agency agreement)

source.quote: Our agreement with the Riverton transit agency requires us to show its service alerts within 2 minutes of publication.

constraints.text: The phone's location never leaves the phone (privacy policy promise)

source.quote: the location never leaves the phone; we say so in our privacy policy

constraints.text: Rework spend capped at $30,000 this year

source.quote: We can put $30,000 into this rework, and not more this year.
First, rush hour must hold up.
Second, lower hosting costs.
Third, less of our scarce time spent on maintenance.

unknowns.question: Will Ashford's feed allow polling every 30 seconds, and in what format is it?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Adding Ashford would add about 400,000 monthly users and a new feed; its limits and format decide the caching and ingestion design.

assumptions.text: Ashford's 400,000 users are a possible addition next year, not current load.
assumptions.why: The brief gives it as the agency's own estimate for a city not yet added.
